notes.RT1: Primary/secondary genres are named and every promised element (bullet-stopping, kung-fu downloads, Agent physics-override) is grounded in the world rules and event refs (ev-045, ev-015, ev-003).
notes.RT2: Three distinct audience groups are each given a why-this-group and a reader-promise tied to concrete set pieces and the simulation/free-will argument.
notes.RT3: Logline and generative_question both carry the dual hook of spectacle and philosophical stakes, and the premise reframes the same question as a personal choice.
notes.RT4: The roster covers all named characters, the Agent class, and key objects/systems (ship, Matrix, Sentinels, hardline, pills), each with a functional role in the plot.
notes.RT5: Five plot briefs each carry who-wants-what, resistance, cost and resolution, and they chain causally from awakening through revival.
notes.RT6: Each plot brief is individually described with specific stakes and costs (identity destruction, failed jump, crew murders) rather than summary.
notes.RT7: Style is defined by named techniques (cause-and-effect action chains, dialogue-carried philosophy, image-carried cost) and reinforced by the forbidden-tics list.
notes.RT8: A three-act structure with five located turning points maps onto the plot briefs, each anchored to specific events (ev-010 through ev-046).
notes.RT9: Five human-experience dilemmas are each staged as opposing sides and anchored to specific events (red pill, steak bargain, revival).
notes.RT10: Identification value links Neo's opening vulnerability (nameless dread, deferential compliance) directly to his admirable strength (refusal of assigned fate) via the same trait.
